newsitem.title: ALBANIA: European Union urges Albania to avoid violence.
newsitem.headline: European Union urges Albania to avoid violence.

text.p: The European Union urged Albanian President Sali Berisha on Friday to postpone as long as possible or avoid altogether a resumption of military activity against armed rebels controlling parts of the south of the country.

"I urged the president to postpone as long as possible or refrain from violence," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo told a news conference after talks with Berisha. "I repeatedly said: 'Make it possible for the European Union to help Albania.'"

Van Mierlo said he had told Berisha the EU favoured fresh elections and a new constitution and said the president was considering such an approach. He said it was up to Albanians to decide whether they wanted change through a new broader-based government or initially through an interim administration.

"It is not this very day that Albania can come to the solutions we hope for," he said. "I had a very frank discussion on this approach and I think that in due course the president will make up his mind on what he has to do."
A two-day suspension of the army's advance on insurgents in the south, approved by Berisha and Albania's major political parties, is in effect until early on Sunday.

But rebels have rejected the appeal and say they will lay down weapons only when Berisha, re-elected this week by parliament to a new five-year term, steps down. Van Mierlo acknowledged that opposition parties had limited influence but urged them to do their utmost to halt violence.
